pronunciation: ngyen-teo (ng as in 'singer'; 'eo' like the 'e' in 'bed' followed by a soft 'oo')
meaning: year; the start of the year; also used for 'years' in the sense of a period (e.g. 'in those years')

example.romanization: Kîn-ngièn ngièn-thèu, ngài hi Thòi-pet tso-kûng.
example.english: At the beginning of this year, I went to Taipei to work.

note: 年頭 literally means 'year head' and is the opposite of 年尾 (ngièn-mî, year's end). Hakka speakers often use these two words to talk about the start and close of the year, such as when settling accounts before the new year.
